subject: Pinnacle Health renewal: uplift sizing, co-term and signer timing
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@pinnaclehealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@pinnaclehealth.com
Date: 2026-07-25T15:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal conversation — uplift sizing and timing

Hi David,

We’re getting ahead of our renewal for the analytics team and expect usage to increase ~2.5x over the next quarter as we onboard two new product lines. Procurement asked me to check whether we can: 

- add capacity mid-contract (true-up topup) and have it co-term with our existing annual renewal
- get a short-term discount while we validate volume before committing to a full year

Key constraints from procurement: we need an amendment routed and signed within the next three weeks to hit FY milestones, and they’ll only approve discounts with an explicit PO number and a finalized amendment. Can you confirm what flexibility Redwood has on staged discounts and whether you can draft an amendment?

Also, we have a security review in process — they may ask for a brief summary of data residency and retention for the uplift.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Product Ops | Pinnacle Health

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@pinnaclehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-25T16:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — uplift sizing and timing

Thanks for the heads up, Alex — appreciate the clarity on timing and procurement requirements. Quick summary / proposal below and I’ve looped in Ben (account lead) and Lauren (rev ops) to confirm commercial and contracting steps.

Proposal options (to match different risk appetites):

1) Staged top-up (low-risk) — immediate mid-contract top-up for projected 2.5x usage, 7% one-time onboarding discount, amendment to co-term at current renewal date. No annual commit change.

2) Acceleration (higher discount) — convert uplift into an annualized add-on (12-month commit for added capacity) and apply 10% discount on the uplift portion. Requires PO and annual amendment; gives best unit economics.

3) Pilot + Convert — 3-month pilot with a smaller top-up and 5% pilot discount; if usage hits the agreed trigger we auto-convert to option (2) with a 10% backdated credit.

Operational notes: 
- We can generate an amendment template today and route via DocuSign; Lauren can attach the PO field so procurement can provide PO# before execution.
- For security: we’ll include a short data residency and retention summary (one-page) as part of the amendment package.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preferred option (1/2/3) and whether procurement needs the PO before or after DocuSign
- Lauren to prepare amendment template and a redline-ready SOW for the uplift
- Ben to validate discount approval path (he’ll confirm ceiling)

I attached a counter quote (Pinnacle_growth_quote_v2.pdf) with line-item math for the three options. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk numbers.

Cheers,
David Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
email: david.kim@redwood.com | office: +1 650-555-0110

David / Lauren — quick notes from my side:

- Margin guardrails: we can approve up to a 10% uplift discount on the added capacity if customer annualizes the uplift (option 2). Anything deeper will need manager sign-off.
- If they want staged/top-up (option 1) we should keep discount at one-time 6–7% and build in an auto-convert trigger.
- For pilot (option 3), require a clear usage trigger (e.g., sustained 70% of projected added tokens over 30 days) and cap the total credit at $XXk.

Lauren — can you prepare amendment template and include (a) PO field, (b) signatory block for Pinnacle, (c) optional auto-convert clause for pilot?

David — I can approve 10% if they sign within the 3-week window and annualize the uplift. If procurement pushes for faster PO routing, we can do preliminary DocuSign hold but require PO before finalizing.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Director | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-26T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — uplift sizing and timing

Thanks all — leaning toward option 2 (annualize the uplift) to lock pricing for the year. Procurement wants the amendment and DocuSign link so they can attach PO# immediately after signature. Two small asks before we execute: 

1) Can you add a clause that the discount only applies to the uplifted capacity (not to baseline units)?
2) Add a 30-day ops exit window if regulatory checks (security review) uncover a blocking item (procurement still needs this for sign-off).

If you can get a DocuSign link with the amendment and the one-page data residency addendum today, I’ll route it to procurement and we’ll aim to sign by next Wednesday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
